persona.who: 66, retired bank officer in Lucknow, wife passed 2 years ago, son in Toronto, daughter in Mumbai. Reads the Gita occasionally, wants to understand it properly.
persona.note: after my wife left us the house is very quiet. children call on sunday. I have time now and I want to read Gita properly not just the shlokas everyone forwards on whatsapp

understanding.bridge: What you are living with is what the texts call searching for what it's all for, and that is where this week begins.
understanding.week_thesis: This week turns the wish to read the Gita properly into a first practice of sitting with one verse until it begins to hold you.

week_beats.hook: You recognise the wish to go beyond the forwarded verse and meet the text on its own terms.
week_beats.diagnose: You see that the forwarded verse is a finger, and the meaning you want is what the text actually teaches about what does not pass.
week_beats.steady: You hold that the self is what the texts point to, and the quiet house is where you can meet it.

queries.hook: The wish to go beyond the forwarded verse and meet the text on its own terms, with the quiet house as your companion.
queries.diagnose: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass, and the texts are what does not pass.
queries.steady: What does not pass is the self, and the self is what the texts point to; the shlokas are a finger, not the moon, but the finger can lead you there.
queries.act: Read one verse at a time, not to understand it all but to sit with one; let the words hold you, and return to them when the quiet feels heavy.
queries.story: An old man who had done everything the world asked of him, sat down with a teacher, and learned that the one who asks is the one who is asked.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna answers Arjuna's question: what does a person of steady mind look like?
verse.sanskrit: या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी । यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः ॥
verse.line: What the crowd sleeps through, the wise stay awake to. What the crowd chases, the wise see past.
verse.translation: What is night for all beings, in that the self-controlled one is awake; and where all beings are awake, that is night for the seeing sage.
verse.why: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

prasang.title: The person of steady wisdom
prasang.summary: Arjuna asks how a steady person speaks, sits and walks. Krishna describes someone content within, unshaken by sorrow, master of the senses, and traces how dwelling on things leads to anger and ruin.
prasang.lesson: Steadiness is built by guarding attention; anger starts with what you dwell on.

verse.meaning: Arjuna asks what a steady mind looks like. Krishna answers that a steady person is awake where others sleep, and sees clearly what others chase. He says the self-controlled are awake in the night of all beings, and where all beings are awake, that is night to the seeing sage. The point is that steadiness is built by guarding attention, and anger starts with what you dwell on.
verse.for_you: You are awake in the quiet house while the world sleeps. Let your attention rest on the one verse before you, and let the forwarded messages fade.

verse.speaker: Prajapati's teaching (narrator)
verse.setting: On the self in the heart that we visit nightly in deep sleep without knowing it.
verse.sanskrit: अनृतापिधानास्तद्यथापि हिरण्यनिधिं निहितमक्षेत्रज्ञा उपर्युपरि सञ्चरन्तो न विन्देयुरेवमेवेमाः सर्वाः प्रजा अहरहर्गच्छन्त्य एतं ब्रह्मलोकं न विन्दन्त्यनृतेन हि प्रत्यूढाः ॥
verse.line: Like people walking daily over buried gold, we pass our own treasure every day and never find it.
verse.translation: As people who do not know the spot walk again and again over a hidden treasure of gold buried in the ground and do not find it, so all these creatures go day after day into that world of Brahman and do not find it, for they are carried away by untruth.

matched.label: Nothing is wrong but nothing feels meaningful

verse.for_you: When life is lived only for what passes, the heart feels empty; meaning is missing when we forget what does not pass.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to the grieving Arjuna, on what in us is never born and never dies.
verse.sanskrit: देहिनोऽस्मिन्यथा देहे कौमारं यौवनं जरा । तथा देहान्तरप्राप्तिर्धीरस्तत्र न मुह्यति ॥
verse.line: Childhood, youth, old age: the body keeps changing. The wise aren't thrown by the next change.
verse.translation: Just as the embodied self passes through childhood, youth and old age in this body, so it passes on to another body. The steady person is not bewildered by this.
verse.why: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

prasang.title: The teaching of the deathless Self (Sankhya)
prasang.summary: Krishna begins his teaching: the self is eternal, bodies change like clothes, and pleasure and pain come and go. Grief for what must pass should not overwhelm us.
prasang.lesson: What you truly are outlasts every loss and every passing pain.

verse.for_you: What passes cannot fill the heart; turning toward what lasts gives each day a quiet purpose.

verse.speaker: Yajnavalkya
verse.setting: Janaka asks what light a person lives by.
verse.sanskrit: अस्तमित आदित्ये याज्ञवल्क्य चन्द्रमस्यस्तमिते शान्तेऽग्नौ किञ्ज्योतिरेवायं पुरुष इति । वागेवास्य ज्योतिर्भवतीति वाचैवायं ज्योतिषास्ते पल्ययते कर्म कुरुते विपल्येतीति । तस्माद्वै सम्राड् अपि यत्र स्वः पाणिर्न विनिर्ज्ञायतेऽथ यत्र वागुच्चरत्युपैव तत्रन्येतीत्येवमेवैतद् याज्ञवल्क्य ॥ अस्तमित आदित्ये याज्ञवल्क्य चन्द्रमस्यस्तमिते शान्तेऽग्नौ शान्तायां वाचि किञ्ज्योतिरेवायं पुरुष इत्यात्मैवास्य ज्योतिर्भवत्यात्मनैवायं ज्योतिषाऽऽस्ते पल्ययते कर्म कुरुते विपल्येतीति ॥
verse.line: When sun, moon and fire are gone and even voices fall silent, the self is your light.
verse.translation: 'When the sun has set, Yajnavalkya, and the moon has set, and the fire has gone out, what light does a person have?' 'Speech is then his light; for when one cannot even see one's own hand, where a voice is heard, there one goes.' 'And when speech too is silent?' 'Then the self is his light. By the light of the self he sits, goes about, works and returns.'
verse.why: When every outer light fails, you still have your own.

prasang.title: Janaka asks: what is our light?
prasang.summary: Yajnavalkya asks the rich, learned King Janaka where he will go when he dies, and the king admits he does not know. Later Janaka asks what light a person lives by: sun, then moon, then fire, then voice, and when all are gone, the self is one's own light.
prasang.lesson: When every outer light fails, you still have your own.

verse.meaning: King Janaka asks what light a person lives by after the sun, moon and fire have gone out. Yajnavalkya says that when even speech is silent, the self is your light. By its light you sit, go about, work and return.
verse.for_you: The quiet house is where every outer light has gone out. Here, in the silence, you do not need to find a new source. You only need to sit with what remains and let it hold you.

verse.speaker: Ashtavakra
verse.setting: Ashtavakra's 'special instruction' to Janaka on why striving and study do not bring peace.
verse.sanskrit: आचक्ष्व श‍ृणु वा तात नानाशास्त्राण्यनेकशः । तथापि न तव स्वास्थ्यं सर्वविस्मरणाद् ऋते ॥
verse.line: Read and recite all the scriptures you like; peace comes when you set them all down.
verse.translation: My son, you may recite or hear many scriptures again and again, but you will not be at ease until you forget them all.
verse.why: Peace isn't another achievement; strain less, and stop expecting escape to fix you.
verse.misuse: Not anti-learning; it warns against mistaking information for peace.

prasang.title: Why striving and study do not bring peace
prasang.summary: Ashtavakra warns that reading scriptures, working or meditating will not bring peace on their own; everyone suffers from straining, and running away from the world doesn't end pain. Even pride in being free is just more suffering.
prasang.lesson: Peace isn't another achievement; strain less, and stop expecting escape to fix you.

verse.meaning: Ashtavakra tells Janaka that you may recite or hear many scriptures again and again, but you will not be at ease until you set them all down. Peace is not another achievement you earn by striving.
verse.for_you: Today, set down the weight of having to understand everything. Let the Gita rest beside you and simply be with what is already here.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna begins his ladder of practices with the simplest instruction.
verse.sanskrit: मय्येव मन आधत्स्व मयि बुद्धिं निवेशय । निवसिष्यसि मय्येव अत ऊर्ध्वं न संशयः ॥
verse.line: Rest your mind in me, settle your thinking in me, and you will live in me.
verse.translation: Fix your mind on me alone, let your understanding settle in me; from then on you will dwell in me. Of this there is no doubt.

matched.label: I want to reconnect with my roots

verse.meaning: Krishna tells Arjuna to fix his mind on him alone and let his understanding settle in him, and then he will dwell in him. This is the simplest and surest path.
verse.for_you: Let your attention rest on one thing today. Not as a task, but as a quiet place to be. Let your mind settle into the stillness of the room and see what it finds there.

story.title: Learned seers find no peace and go to Ganesha
story.story_hook: They knew every verse of every Veda, and still could not sleep.
story.summary: Seers who had received all the Vedas still found no peace, so they went to Ganesha's world and took refuge in him. Ganesha tells them that though he has no form, loving devotees see him in the form they long for, and that knowing his highest form brings lasting peace.
story.lesson: Learning alone may not settle the heart; turning to God can.

anchor.setting: Seers who had studied every Veda come to Ganesha's world because learning alone left them restless.
anchor.sanskrit: अतो नेवाभवच्छान्तिरस्माकं चेतसि प्रभो!। वयं शरणमापन्ना भवल्लोकमुपस्थिताः ॥
anchor.line: Lord, no peace came to our minds. So we have come to you for refuge.
anchor.translation: So no peace came into our minds, Lord. We have come to your world and taken refuge in you.

story.teaser: The seers knew every verse of every Veda, and still couldn't sleep
story.for_you: You have spent a lifetime gathering knowledge, much like those seers. Today, let that same devotion turn toward the silence you are entering. See if your practice can rest not in knowing, but in the quiet act of looking.

script: The house is quiet and you are reading. You are not looking for a quick comfort today. You want to know what a steady mind actually looks like, as Krishna describes it to Arjuna.

Arjuna is on the battlefield. He asks Krishna what a steady person looks like, how they speak and sit. Krishna tells him that the self-controlled are awake when all beings are in the night of delusion, and that where the crowd chases, the seeing sage looks past that. And Krishna replied:
या निशा सर्वभूतानां तस्यां जागर्ति संयमी, यस्यां जाग्रति भूतानि सा निशा पश्यतो मुनेः.
In plain words: What the crowd sleeps through, the wise stay awake to. What the crowd chases, the wise see past.

This is not about sleeping less. It is about what you attend to when the world goes quiet. The crowd chases noise and distraction, and they call that being awake. The steady person is awake to what actually matters, while the crowd sleeps through it. This is harder than it sounds, because the mind wants to wander back to what it has lost or what it fears. Steadiness is built by choosing where you put your attention, and anger starts when you dwell on things that pull you away from the truth.
In the quiet house this morning, let your attention rest on this one verse. Let the forwarded messages fade, and let your mind stay awake to what is actually here.
What is the one thing you are chasing that you might let the seeing sage look past?

depth.life: You sit in the quiet house after the calls end. The forwarded verses offered a familiar shape, but they did not hold. Now you are reaching for the actual text, wanting to meet the Gita where it lives, not in the clipped lines others send.
depth.points: The texts show that steadiness is not a feeling but a habit of attention. Most people are asleep to what matters, chasing noise. A steady mind is awake to what is real, and it stays awake by choosing what to dwell on.
depth.practice: Read the verse aloud once, then let the book close and sit with the image of night and waking for a full minute.
depth.question: What is the one thing you have been dwelling on that you could gently turn away from today?
